lesson_title: The Tuck-Shop Test: Where Factories Choose to Live
hook_text: Why does the sugar mill live with the cane, but the brewery lives with you?
clip_script: Every industry answers one playground question: what is more of a pain to move — what the business uses, or what it sells? The school tuck-shop sits inside the school because its customers cannot travel and its product must be fresh. A sugar mill sits among the cane fields, because cane is a heavy, fast-rotting monster that boils down to a small bag of sugar — you move the light sugar, never the heavy cane. Bread goes stale and beer is mostly heavy glass, so the ovens and breweries sit in the city with the customers. One question, and the factory always sits at the difficult end.
visual_style: Split-screen tug-of-war: cane trucks versus sugar bags, flour sacks versus fresh loaves, with factories sliding along the rope to the heavier end.
pacing: Snappy question, two quick contrasts, satisfying rule at the end.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson — five industry types, eight location factors, one test that sorts them all.
